before_code: The *Hecke coset module* data underlying abstract Hecke rings: the compatibility class IsHeckeTriple Δ H₁ H₂ — a submonoid Δ and subgroups with H₁, H₂ ≤ Δ ≤ commensurator ... the Hecke coset module 𝕋 Δ H₁ H₂ Z of finitely-supported Z-linear combinations ... The data enters unbundled ... The convolution product 𝕋 Δ H₁ H₂ R × 𝕋 Δ H₂ H₃ R → 𝕋 Δ H₁ H₃ R and the ring structure ... land in follow-up PRs. _Prepared by Claude._  [~230 words, 2 dense paragraphs, grew each round]
after_code:
Adds the unbundled data underlying abstract Hecke rings, following Shimura (Ch. 3) and Krieg (Ch. I):
- IsHeckeTriple Δ H₁ H₂: the compatibility class on Δ and subgroups H₁, H₂ ...
- HeckeCoset Δ H₁ H₂: the double cosets H₁\Δ/H₂.
- HeckeCosetModule Δ H₁ H₂ Z: their finitely-supported Z-linear combinations, with 𝕋 Δ H Z the diagonal Hecke ring.
The convolution product and ring structure follow in later PRs.  [~80 words]
description: Reviewer (loefflerd, PR #41251): 'As so often happens with AI-generated PRs, the PR description is getting longer and longer with each iteration. Please keep it a bit more to the point, & train your agent to do this automatically in future.' Keep mathlib PR descriptions SHORT: a one-line summary + a few concrete bullets naming the main declarations. Do NOT let the description grow/accrete with each round of edits — when addressing feedback, RE-TIGHTEN the description rather than appending to it. Also keep it factually in sync with the code (e.g. once 𝕋 was reserved for the diagonal ring HeckeRing Δ H Z, stop calling the general module '𝕋 Δ H₁ H₂ Z'). Mirrors the /fix-pr-feedback skill's 'PR description' rules.
